canonical_name: Kurosh subgroup-decomposition theorem family for free products
literal_source_claim_en: The structure of subgroups of free products.
source_attribution: Alexander Kurosh, 1934 (catalog metadata; exact source-to-claim identity remains unaccepted)
canonical_statement: Source candidate pending independent review: if G is the free product of an arbitrary family of component subgroups H_alpha, every subgroup F of G admits a free-product decomposition F = *_{beta} F_beta in which each factor F_beta is either infinite cyclic or conjugate in G to a subgroup of some component H_alpha.
canonical_claim: Provisionally source-identified human claim only; not yet the master-accepted canonical claim or an exact Lean proposition.
statement_blocker: The primary 1934 headline has been located: every subgroup of a free product can be decomposed as a free product whose factors are infinite cyclic or conjugate to subgroups of components. Exact Lean freeze still requires independent transcription and translation review, incorporated free-product and conjugacy definitions, universe and carrier choices, an exact encoding of 'can be decomposed', factor-family and boundary conventions, and checked transports for stronger modern formulations. Adding double-coset indexing, a packaged free factor, or uniqueness to the source root would broaden it.
domain_and_universes: Source scope: an arbitrary family of component subgroups H_alpha whose free product is G, and an arbitrary subgroup F of G. Lean universes, external-versus-internal free-product encoding, subgroup carrier transports, existential factor index, and decomposition-equivalence codomain remain to be frozen.
conclusion: Source headline: F admits a free-product decomposition into factors each of which is either infinite cyclic or conjugate to a subgroup of one component H_alpha. The exact Lean representation of decomposition and conjugacy remains open; double-coset indexing, a packaged free factor, uniqueness, and rank are not part of the located headline.
